decisive_items: lytic destruction with cortical fracture of the T1 and T2 vertebrae
lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
response.rationale: Young adult with aggressive thoracic/pleural-based mass and lytic vertebral destruction strongly favors Ewing's sarcoma, which commonly presents with bone destruction and soft tissue mass. Lymphoma remains plausible but lacks the specific bony lytic pattern.

rejected.why: Thymoma is typically anterior mediastinal, less likely to present with this pleural/vertebral destructive pattern without classic associations.
Germ cell tumor is rare in young women and less compatible with the osseous destruction and pleural origin.
Castleman disease is less likely than malignancy given aggressive bony erosion and acute deterioration.
Lymphoma can cause mediastinal mass and constitutional symptoms, but the prominent vertebral lytic destruction and pleural/operculum origin favor Ewing's sarcoma.
